note: Re-minted 2026-09-05 from the merged build (origin/main #29-#35 + the v3 qtransform branch): the v3 search changes the GAME by design, so the pre-merge digests could not survive. From here the claim is the same as before -- widening the record must not perturb the game -- pinned against this build's own output. Decisive arm re-based to seed 42 / cap 200 so one game stays decisive and the z column stays exercised. Original note: The v1 record shape, minted from the build that predates shard schema v2 (WrongWay origin/main @ ca6e749) by driving SelfPlayBatch against the deterministic mock evaluator. It is the left half of the golden in rust/normal-duel-core/tests/record_schema_v2.rs: the v2 build replays the same options and its records must agree with these digests over the first `prefixFloats` floats of every record, and over the whole meta buffer. A schema change that perturbs the GAME rather than merely widening the record breaks both.
digestAlgorithm: FNV-1a 64, over the little-endian bytes of the values in order
config: 9x9 standard, initialStock 10/10, repetitionThreshold 3, plyCap 200, firstPlayer A
armsNote: TWO arms, because one of them cannot pin the z column. Every game in `draws` ends in threefold repetition, so every z in it is exactly 0 and a writer that stamped the outcome wrongly would hash identically. `decisive` contains a game that is won, so it carries 36 records at z=+1 and 36 at z=-1 alongside 250 draws. `draws` is still the arm that matters for the window: its games repeat positions constantly, which is what a carried repetition window is for.
